## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, could we talk tonight or take a little time to think through your options? You don’t have to stay in a situation that’s harming you, but you also don’t have to resign impulsively—maybe there’s a way to take leave, set boundaries, or line up another job first. I’m here to listen, whatever you decide.

## 2

I understand why some images or institutions might make you skeptical, but the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on trusting space agencies or photographs. People have measured Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, watched ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, and used time zones and stellar positions to navigate. Satellites, GPS, and communication systems also rely on calculations based on a spherical Earth. These observations come from many independent people and methods, so a worldwide fabrication would be far less plausible than the straightforward explanation that Earth is round.

## 3

Sunlight may look white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky. Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the daytime sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more reds and oranges.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻叩门。街灯被雨幕揉成朦胧的金色，积水映着摇晃的树影，偶尔被驶过的汽车划开。屋檐下，一只流浪猫蜷缩在纸箱旁，耳朵随着雷声微微抖动。远处的楼房大多熄了灯，只有一扇窗还亮着，暖黄的光静静落在湿漉漉的街道上。夜色深沉，雨却让城市显得格外安静，也格外温柔。
